problem: Latent semantic grid maps built from VLM embeddings (VLMaps, OpenScene) are only evaluated anecdotally or via downstream navigation success, so the quality of the embedding representation itself is not rigorously measured or comparable across methods.
motivation: Open-vocabulary maps are increasingly used for robot navigation and human interaction, but downstream success does not reveal the limits of the representation. The paper proposes quality measures for queryability and distinctness, plus resolution analysis, since map size depends on cell size.
key_idea: Evaluate latent semantic maps with per-query binary queryability metrics plus intra-map (dispersion ratio) and inter-map (Wasserstein distance) distinctness measures, and study their dependence on map resolution.
insight: 3D-aware OpenScene features with LSeg give the best queryability and distinctness, but they are not scale invariant: F1 drops quickly with coarser cells, while image-based VLMaps features stay stable across resolutions. The low F1 of VLMaps-style querying (against the single 'other' string), even with prompt engineering (+0.059 F1 LSeg, +0.008 OpenSeg), shows open-vocabulary thresholding is an unsolved problem. The inter-map median ratios (6.31, 3.78, 2.07, 1.42) follow the same ordering as queryability.
method: Queryability: each query yields a binary voxel mask compared to the ground-truth mask, and precision, recall, F1 and IoU are averaged over maps and queries (accuracy is avoided because true negatives dominate).
Intra-map distinctness: ratio of the average absolute deviation (cosine distance to the mean embedding) of a class's embeddings to that of all map embeddings; lower is more distinct.

Inter-map distinctness: closed-form Wasserstein-2 distance between Gaussian approximations of same-label and different-label embedding sets across maps; compare the medians of the matching and non-matching distributions.

Query protocols: VLMaps querying (cosine similarity to the query vs 'other', then closing, blur, threshold, dilation), applied to both methods, plus closed-set semantic segmentation by label equality; prompt-engineering ablation.

Setup: 10 Matterport3D sequences (as in VLMaps) with 40 labels; VLMaps 3D mapping vs OpenScene 2D-3D ensemble; LSeg (CLIP ViT-B/32) and OpenSeg (ViT-L/14) encoders; resolutions 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 m; instance ground truth from region growing.

setting.backbone: Pretrained LSeg and OpenSeg (CLIP-based) encoders with VLMaps and OpenScene mapping (frozen, evaluation only)
setting.training_data: none (evaluation study using the authors' pretrained encoders)
setting.observation: RGB-D sequences from Matterport3D (posed, simulated via Habitat)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth semantic maps from Matterport3D are used for evaluation only

numbers_note: No navigation-benchmark results; the paper reports map-quality metrics (queryability F1/IoU etc.) on 10 Matterport3D sequences, which do not fit the canonical navigation benchmarks. Resolution results are given only in figures.
results: In semantic segmentation, OpenScene+LSeg is best (F1 0.645, IoU 0.480) vs VLMaps+LSeg (F1 0.541, IoU 0.375). With VLMaps querying, VLMaps+LSeg is best (F1 0.425, IoU 0.271), while OpenScene gets F1 0.174 (LSeg) and 0.111 (OpenSeg), with very high recall and low precision. OpenScene is more distinct within and across maps, but its performance drops when resolution changes.
limitations: Only two mapping methods and two encoders on 10 Matterport3D sequences with 40 closed-set labels; open-vocabulary queries are demonstrated only qualitatively.
Object-level and point-cloud maps (ConceptGraphs, HOV-SG) are not evaluated, and the Gaussian approximation is used for the Wasserstein distance.
Ground-truth instances come from region growing on semantics; OpenScene had to be adapted to VLMaps querying.
